locator: Statistical section, 'Water Supply Sources, Demand and Capacity Information (Continued)', printed p. 129 (PDF p. 147), block 'CITY DIVISION', columns 2022 and 2025
shows: Lehigh County Authority's ten-year table of supply and demand gives, for the City Division (the Allentown water system that LCA leases from the City), an average daily demand and a maximum daily demand in gallons for each year from 2016 to 2025. The highest maximum day in the ten years is 30,870,900 gallons in 2022, a year with an average daily demand of 22,504,438 gallons; their ratio is 1.3718 (derived). In 2025 the figures are 22,903,498 and 30,084,400 gallons (ratio 1.3135, derived). The estimated safe yield of supplies is 71,000,000 gallons a day in every year. The same figures appear in million gallons a day in the table 'Operating and Capital Indicators' on printed p. 133 (22.50 and 30.87 MGD in 2022; 22.90 and 30.08 MGD in 2025).
limits: Self-reported by the utility in its financial report. The demand is the water that the City Division produces, which includes the water sold to LCA's own Suburban Division and to the neighbouring townships; the table does not split it. The maximum day is the highest day of each year in a ten-year window, not of the whole record. The safe yield is a source yield, not a treatment capacity. The page is printed sideways: in the text layer the four values of each City Division year (average, maximum, safe yield, surplus) run together without spaces, so each quote is one such run; the surplus equals the safe yield less the maximum day, which confirms how the run splits.
